title: Liangzhu culture emerges
description: A stratified Neolithic society arises in the Yangtze delta that, until about 2300 BCE, builds a walled city and large waterworks and makes elaborate ritual jades.

title: Erlitou culture
description: A large settlement with palace compounds and bronze foundries rises on the Yi and Luo rivers, widely seen as China's first state-level society and often linked to the traditional Xia.

title: Erlitou culture
description: A Bronze Age centre with palaces and bronze workshops rises in the Yellow River valley; some scholars identify it with the Xia dynasty of the later histories.

title: Zhengzhou Shang City
description: Builders of the Erligang culture raise a walled city with rammed-earth walls about seven kilometres around, an early capital of the Shang.

title: Zhengzhou Shang city
description: A rammed-earth walled city grows at modern Zhengzhou, often identified as an early Shang capital, of the first culture to cast bronze vessels widely in China.

title: Oracle bone inscriptions
description: Diviners of the Shang kings carve questions on bones and turtle shells, the earliest substantial body of Chinese writing.

title: Tomb of Fu Hao
description: Fu Hao, consort of King Wu Ding and a military leader named on oracle bones, is buried with hundreds of bronzes and jades; the tomb was found intact in 1976.

title: Sanxingdui sacrificial pits
description: A Bronze Age culture in Sichuan, distinct from the Shang, buries bronze masks, figures and trees in sacrificial pits.

title: Battle of Muye
description: King Wu of Zhou defeats the Shang, founding the longest-lasting Chinese dynasty.

title: Birth of Confucius
description: The teacher whose ideas on duty, family and government shape Chinese society for two and a half thousand years is born in the state of Lu.

title: Battle of Changping
description: Qin destroys the army of Zhao, clearing the way for its conquest of the other states.

title: Qin unification
description: The state of Qin conquers its last rival and its king takes the title of First Emperor.

title: Han dynasty founded
description: Liu Bang becomes emperor; the Han rule, with one interruption, for four centuries.

title: Zhang Qian sets out for the west
description: Emperor Wu's envoy travels to Central Asia, and his reports open the routes later called the Silk Road.

title: Han Protectorate of the Western Regions
description: After Xiongnu forces in the west submit, the Han appoint Zheng Ji protector-general over the oasis states of the Tarim Basin, the first direct Chinese rule in what is now Xinjiang.

title: Cai Lun presents papermaking
description: The court official is credited with the method of making paper from bark, hemp and rags.

title: Battle of Red Cliffs
description: Cao Cao's southward advance is defeated; the exact site is disputed.

title: End of the Han dynasty
description: Cao Pi forces the last Han emperor to abdicate, and China divides into the Three Kingdoms.

title: Battle of Fei River
description: The Eastern Jin defeat a much larger northern army, keeping the south independent.

title: Sui reunifies China
description: The Sui conquer the Chen dynasty in the south, ending nearly three centuries of division.

title: Tang dynasty founded
description: Li Yuan takes the throne after the fall of the Sui.

title: Songtsen Gampo founds the Tibetan Empire
description: The Yarlung king Songtsen Gampo unites the peoples of the Tibetan Plateau into an empire and later moves his capital to Lhasa.

title: Battle of Talas
description: An Abbasid army defeats the Tang, marking the limit of Chinese expansion into Central Asia.

title: An Lushan rebellion begins
description: A frontier general's revolt starts eight years of war that permanently weaken the Tang.

title: Diamond Sutra printed
description: A woodblock scroll found at Dunhuang is the oldest dated printed book.

title: Song dynasty founded
description: Zhao Kuangyin is made emperor by his troops and reunifies most of China.

title: First government paper money
description: The Song state takes over the jiaozi notes issued by Sichuan merchants and prints the first series of government paper money.

title: Bi Sheng invents movable type
description: The artisan Bi Sheng makes movable type of fired clay, one piece for each character, the first known movable-type printing, described by the scholar Shen Kuo.

title: Wang Anshi's New Policies
description: Emperor Shenzong appoints Wang Anshi, who launches reforms of state loans to farmers, taxation, trade and the army that divide the court for decades.

title: Quanzhou maritime trade supervisorate
description: The Song open an office of the maritime trade bureau at the Fujian port, which grows into one of the world's largest seaports, praised by Marco Polo and Ibn Battuta.

title: Fall of Kaifeng
description: The Jurchen Jin capture the Song capital and two emperors, and the Song court moves south.

title: Lin'an becomes the Southern Song capital
description: After the loss of the north the Song court settles at Lin'an (Hangzhou), which grows into one of the largest and richest cities in the world.

title: Yuan dynasty proclaimed
description: Kublai Khan gives his realm a Chinese dynastic name.

title: Battle of Yamen
description: The last Song fleet is destroyed and the Mongol conquest of China is complete.

title: Ming dynasty founded
description: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming and drives the Yuan court north later that year.

title: Zheng He's first voyage
description: The first of seven treasure-fleet expeditions sets out across the Indian Ocean.

title: Capital moved to Beijing
description: The Yongle Emperor moves the Ming capital to Beijing, where the Forbidden City has just been completed.

title: Portuguese settle at Macau
description: Ming officials allow Portuguese traders a permanent base, the first European settlement in China.

title: Battle of Shanhai Pass
description: Manchu forces pass the Great Wall and go on to take Beijing; Qing rule over China begins.

title: Li Zicheng takes Beijing
description: Rebel armies under Li Zicheng enter the capital and the Chongzhen Emperor hangs himself on Coal Hill, ending the Ming dynasty in Beijing.

title: Yangzhou massacre
description: Qing forces under Prince Dodo sack Yangzhou after its defence by the Ming loyalist Shi Kefa and kill a large part of its people over ten days.

title: Revolt of the Three Feudatories
description: Wu Sangui and two other Chinese princes who held the south for the Qing rebel when the Kangxi Emperor moves to abolish their fiefs; their defeat secures Qing rule.

title: Treaty of Nerchinsk
description: The Qing and Russia fix their border in the first treaty between China and a European power.

title: Qing army enters Lhasa
description: A Qing expedition drives the Dzungars out of Tibet and installs the Seventh Dalai Lama, beginning nearly two centuries of Qing overlordship.

title: Qing conquest of Dzungaria
description: The Qianlong Emperor's armies destroy the Dzungar Khanate, killing most of the Dzungar people, and go on to take the Tarim Basin.

title: Macartney embassy
description: The Qianlong Emperor receives Britain's envoy and refuses his requests for wider trade.

title: White Lotus Rebellion begins
description: A rising inspired by White Lotus teachings and tax grievances breaks out in the mountains between Sichuan, Hubei and Shaanxi, and takes the Qing eight years to crush.

title: Destruction of opium at Humen
description: Commissioner Lin Zexu destroys more than a thousand tons of confiscated British opium, the trigger for the First Opium War.

title: Treaty of Nanjing
description: Ends the First Opium War, ceding Hong Kong Island and opening treaty ports.

title: Taiping Rebellion begins
description: Hong Xiuquan proclaims the Heavenly Kingdom; the civil war that follows kills at least twenty million people.

title: Old Summer Palace burned
description: British troops destroy the imperial gardens at the end of the Second Opium War.

title: Yakub Beg rules Kashgaria
description: Amid the wider revolt against Qing rule, the Kokandi officer Yakub Beg takes Kashgar and founds the state of Yettishar in the Tarim Basin.

title: Qing reconquest of Xinjiang
description: The armies of Zuo Zongtang retake the cities of Xinjiang over two years after the death of Yakub Beg, and the Qing later make the region a province.

title: Xinjiang becomes a province
description: After retaking the region from Yakub Beg, the Qing make Xinjiang a regular province with its capital at Dihua.

title: Allied armies take Beijing
description: Troops of eight nations relieve the foreign legations besieged during the Boxer Uprising, and the court flees.

title: Wuchang Uprising
description: An army mutiny sets off the revolution that ends the Qing dynasty.

title: Republic of China founded
description: Sun Yat-sen is inaugurated provisional president, and the last emperor abdicates six weeks later.

title: May Fourth Movement
description: Student protests against the Versailles settlement grow into a wider cultural and political movement.

title: Chinese Communist Party founded
description: Thirteen delegates hold the party's first congress in the French Concession.

title: Shanghai massacre
description: Chiang Kai-shek turns on his Communist allies, beginning the civil war between the two parties.

title: Long March begins
description: The Red Army breaks out of its encircled base and retreats for a year to the north-west, during which Mao Zedong becomes its leader.

title: Marco Polo Bridge incident
description: A clash between Chinese and Japanese troops opens full-scale war.

title: Nanjing Massacre
description: Japanese troops take the capital and over six weeks kill great numbers of civilians and prisoners.

title: People's Republic proclaimed
description: Mao Zedong announces the founding of the People's Republic of China.

title: People's Republic takes over Xinjiang
description: After the Nationalist provincial authorities defect and the Three Districts leaders accede to Beijing, People's Liberation Army units enter Ürümqi and Xinjiang joins the People's Republic.

title: Battle of Chamdo
description: The People's Liberation Army defeats the Tibetan army in the east, forcing Lhasa to accept the Seventeen Point Agreement in 1951.

title: Seventeen Point Agreement
description: Representatives of the Tibetan local government and the central government sign the Seventeen Point Agreement on the peaceful liberation of Tibet, bringing Tibet under Chinese sovereignty while promising it regional autonomy.

title: Great Leap Forward
description: A campaign of forced collectivisation and backyard industry leads to a famine that kills tens of millions.

title: Tibetan uprising
description: Protests in Lhasa turn into a revolt that the army crushes; the Dalai Lama flees to India, where he sets up a government in exile.

title: Dalai Lama flees to India
description: After days of protest and fighting in Lhasa, the 14th Dalai Lama slips out of the city and crosses the Himalayas to India, where he is granted asylum.

title: First nuclear test
description: China explodes its first atomic bomb.

title: Cultural Revolution begins
description: A party circular drafted under Mao launches a decade of purges, Red Guard violence and upheaval.

title: Nixon visits China
description: The American president meets Mao, ending more than twenty years without relations between the two countries.

title: Tangshan earthquake
description: An earthquake levels the city and kills at least 240,000 people.

title: Death of Mao Zedong
description: Mao dies after ruling China for 27 years, and the Gang of Four are arrested a month later.

title: Reform and opening up
description: At the Third Plenum of the Central Committee, Deng Xiaoping's line of economic reform replaces class struggle as the party's priority.

title: Shenzhen Special Economic Zone
description: The first of the special economic zones of the reform era is established.

title: Tiananmen Square protests suppressed
description: The army clears weeks of student-led protests from central Beijing by force.

title: Handover of Hong Kong
description: Britain returns Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty.

title: China joins the World Trade Organization
description: Membership after fifteen years of negotiation ties China into world trade.

title: Sichuan earthquake
description: An earthquake of magnitude 7.9 kills nearly 70,000 people.

title: Beijing Olympics
description: The Summer Olympics open in Beijing.

title: Ürümqi riots
description: A protest by Uyghurs turns into ethnic violence between Uyghurs and Han Chinese in which nearly two hundred people die, followed by a sweeping security crackdown.

title: Xi Jinping takes office
description: Xi Jinping was elected president, having taken over as Communist Party and military leader the previous November.

title: Belt and Road Initiative announced
description: Xi Jinping proposed the Silk Road Economic Belt in a speech in Kazakhstan, the start of what became the Belt and Road Initiative.

title: One-child policy ends
description: The Communist Party announced the end of the one-child policy, allowing all couples two children from the following year.

title: Hong Kong protests
description: Hundreds of thousands marched against a proposed extradition law, the start of the largest protest movement in Hong Kong's history.

title: COVID-19 outbreak in Wuhan
description: A new coronavirus is identified in Wuhan; it spreads into a pandemic that kills millions worldwide.

title: Hong Kong national security law
description: Beijing imposes a security law on Hong Kong that criminalises secession and subversion and ends the protest movement.

title: Beijing Winter Olympics
description: Beijing becomes the first city to have hosted both the Summer and the Winter Olympics.

title: Xi Jinping's third term
description: The 20th Party Congress gives Xi Jinping a third term as general secretary, breaking the two-term norm.

title: Zero-COVID policy ends
description: After protests sparked by a fatal fire in Ürümqi, the government drops most of its lockdown rules.
